Maya (CS): PlumBank escalation — identical rerank payloads returning different scores after last night's runtime patch. Two request IDs: req-4721a, req-4721b. Customer says payloads byte-for-byte identical. They see rank swap between candidates 3 and 4. Raising here to triage.

deploy-bot: Deployed runtime/v1.12.4 -> runtime/v1.12.5 at 2026-03-05T03:12Z :arrow_up: (note: rollout included tokenizer whitespace normalization change)

Aj Patel: looking. Which model + model_version did they call? Are they pinning? Also paste exact rerank params (max_candidates, temperature, normalize_whitespace flag)

Maya (CS): payload:
```
{"query":"how to dispute a transaction","candidates":["Check your statement","Contact support","File a claim","Review merchant policy"],"max_candidates":100}
```
Model: rerank-v2.1 (not pinned). Region: us-west-2. Both requests returned 200 but scores differ: req-4721a scores: [0.92,0.88,0.76,0.74] req-4721b scores: [0.92,0.88,0.74,0.76]

Ravi (ML): quick thought — we pushed a whitespace normalization tweak in token-encoder yesterday that could change token boundaries. Combined with batching/KV cache behavior that might affect ordering FP accumulation, could explain tiny score flips that reorder ties. Can you share raw request bytes or base64 of both calls?

Maya (CS): uploading artifacts to secure link: https://redwood-secure/artifacts/plumbank/req-4721a.gz and req-4721b.gz. Customer insists no client change. Latency: req-4721a 1.2s, req-4721b 2.7s. No 5xxs. Customer asks for immediate mitigation and SLA credit if systemic.

Sam (SRE): logs show both requests hit different workers and different batch windows. Snippet:
```
[worker-7] batch_size=8 order=[req-4719,req-4720,req-4721a] kv_cache_cleared=false
[worker-12] batch_size=12 order=[req-4721b,req-4722,...] kv_cache_cleared=true
```
Worker-12 had a cache refresh during the window.

Aj Patel: hypothesis — batching + cache-clear path causes non-deterministic floating point accumulation order, producing tiny score diffs that flip close ranks. Ravi, can you run deterministic rerank with forced batch boundaries and KV cache cleared flag? Also confirm whether whitespace normalization affects token ids for this query.

Ravi (ML): running deterministic unit with fixed RNG/kernels now (rerank-repro-981). If we reproduce, mitigation options: 1) pin tenant to rerank-v2.0 (pre-normalization), 2) make KV cache clear deterministic during batching, 3) revert normalization change.

Maya (CS): PlumBank wants an immediate workaround — can we pin them to rerank-v2.0 while you investigate? They rely on stable ranks for fraud scoring. :pray:

Aj Patel: agree. Creating a tenant routing override: tenant=plumbank -> model=rerank-v2.0, rollout id roll-9833. Applying now and will monitor.

Maya (CS): thanks — I'll update customer and open an SLA ticket. Scheduling tech sync with PlumBank at 11:30 PT. Will add legal for credit discussion.

Ravi (ML): repro job shows rank flip reproducible when kv_cache_cleared=true and batch orders differ; magnitude ~2e-4. Filing issue INF-6729. Next steps: patch batching path to enforce deterministic reduction order and add a non-regression test.

Aj Patel: noted. I'll follow up with a hotfix PR and coordinate canary.

Maya (CS): appreciated — keeping customer posted.
